newsitem.title: USA: GM's fourth quarter income slashed by strikes.
newsitem.headline: GM's fourth quarter income slashed by strikes.

text.p: General Motors Corp. Tuesday reported fourth quarter income of $786 million, less than half of the $1.87 billion it earned a year ago, as labor woes in the United States and Canada took $700 million out of profits.
The world's largest automaker said it earned 92 cents a share, down from $1.98 a year earlier. Revenue fell to $40.9 billion from $41.4 billion.

"Clearly our 1996 fourth-quarter and calendar-year results were impacted by the strike-related production losses in the United States and Canada and are not indicative of GM's potential for continued profit improvement," GM Chairman John F. Smith Jr., said.

GM's North American Operations, its core automotive group in the U.S., had a net loss of $124 million, versus a profit of $603 million in the year-ago quarter. For the year, the North American unit earned $1.2 billion, down from $2.4 billion.

The automaker's International Operations reported net income of $353 million for the quarter, down from a profit of $498 million a year ago. For all of 1996, GM's international profits were $1.5 billion, down from $1.6 billion in 1995.
For the year, GM earned $5.0 billion, or $6.06 a share, down from $6.9 billion, or $7.21 a share. Revenue for the year rose to $164.1 billion from $160.3 billion.
